title: Firewall Rule Audit — Spot the Misconfiguration
context: You are a network security engineer. Meridian Hospital's firewall configuration has been exported for a security review. Use shell commands to audit the rules, find dangerously permissive entries, and identify the misconfigured rule that violates least-privilege. Type each command and press Enter.
description: Audit Meridian Hospital's exported firewall rules. Use grep and cat to identify rules that allow unrestricted access to internal services, pinpoint exposed admin ports, and flag the misconfigured rule.
hint: Use 'cat firewall_rules.csv' to read all rules. Use 'grep "0.0.0.0" firewall_rules.csv' to find rules with ANY source. Use 'grep -E "22|3306|5432" firewall_rules.csv' to find exposed admin ports. The hidden flag is base64-encoded: type 'base64 -d hidden_flag.b64' to reveal it.
starterCode:
#!/bin/bash
# ============================================
# SENTINEL SECURITY LAB: Firewall Audit
# Meridian General Hospital — Network Review
# ============================================
# Evidence files available:
#   firewall_rules.csv   - Exported firewall rules
#   service_map.txt      - Port-to-service mapping
#   risk_matrix.txt      - Risk levels for exposures
#   hidden_flag.b64      - Encoded flag
#
# Start with: cat firewall_rules.csv
# Then work through each task below.
# ============================================
echo "=== FIREWALL AUDIT STARTED ==="
ls

additionalFiles.name: service_map.txt
additionalFiles.content:
=== PORT-TO-SERVICE MAPPING ===
Common admin and sensitive ports:

PORT  | SERVICE        | RISK IF EXPOSED TO INTERNET
------+----------------+----------------------------
22    | SSH            | CRITICAL -- brute force, credential theft
23    | Telnet         | CRITICAL -- plaintext credentials
80    | HTTP           | MEDIUM   -- acceptable for web servers
443   | HTTPS          | MEDIUM   -- acceptable for web servers
3306  | MySQL          | CRITICAL -- database direct exposure
5432  | PostgreSQL     | CRITICAL -- database direct exposure
5900  | VNC            | CRITICAL -- remote desktop, full control
8080  | HTTP-alt       | HIGH     -- often unpatched dev services
3389  | RDP            | CRITICAL -- remote desktop, ransomware vector

PRINCIPLE OF LEAST PRIVILEGE:
  Firewall rules should restrict SOURCE to the minimum required IP range.
  ANY SOURCE (0.0.0.0/0) for admin ports is a critical misconfiguration.

additionalFiles.name: risk_matrix.txt
additionalFiles.content:
=== FIREWALL RISK MATRIX ===
Framework: CIS Benchmark for Network Security

CRITICAL RISK INDICATORS:
  - Admin port (22, 3389, 5900) exposed to 0.0.0.0/0 (any IP)
  - Database port (3306, 5432) exposed to 0.0.0.0/0
  - Unrestricted outbound rules (potential data exfiltration path)

RISK SCORING:
  0.0.0.0/0 source on admin port = RISK SCORE: 25 (CRITICAL)
  0.0.0.0/0 source on DB port    = RISK SCORE: 20 (CRITICAL)
  Restricted subnet on admin port = RISK SCORE: 8  (MEDIUM)
  Restricted subnet on HTTP/S     = RISK SCORE: 3  (LOW)

MOST DANGEROUS MISCONFIGURATION:
  An SSH rule (port 22) with source 0.0.0.0/0 allows any attacker
  on the internet to attempt to log into your server.
  This is the #1 cause of server compromises.

tasks.title: Start the audit
tasks.desc: Type: ls — lists all files in this audit environment. (This runs automatically when the lab loads.)

tasks.title: Read all firewall rules
tasks.desc: Type: cat firewall_rules.csv — displays the full exported firewall configuration. How many rules are there?

tasks.title: Find any-source rules
tasks.desc: Type: grep "0.0.0.0/0" firewall_rules.csv — finds rules that allow access from ANY IP address on the internet.

tasks.title: Identify exposed admin ports
tasks.desc: Type: grep -E "22|3306|5900" firewall_rules.csv — finds rules for high-risk admin and database ports.

tasks.title: Look up the risk level
tasks.desc: Type: grep "SSH" service_map.txt — check what risk level an exposed SSH port carries.

tasks.title: Flag the misconfigured rule
tasks.desc: RULE-004 allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0 — the most dangerous rule. Type: echo "VULN: RULE-004 exposes SSH to ANY SOURCE"

tasks.title: Decode the hidden flag
tasks.desc: Type: base64 -d hidden_flag.b64 — decodes and reveals your lab flag. Copy the FLAG{...} and submit it above.
